claims.claim: Bootstrap attests the imported legacy distribution in an isolated interpreter, checks its installed operator path and exact VCS commit, and excludes synchronized source from that witness.

The bootstrap accepts only the fixed first reviewed migration-capable target and an exact intent bound to the repository, control commits, pin blobs, TASK identity, and Executor. It writes one handoff record that only the bound target checkout can consume.

Bootstrap delegates execution to the existing migrate-primary handoff and Runtime path. Re-entry checks the recorded handoff and RUN state; completed bootstrap handoffs cannot be reused. Pre-handoff rejection creates no RUN. Rejected target cleanup now removes read-only Git objects on Windows without masking the original rejection.

The implementation uses repository-bound intent without downstream-specific execution policy. Tests cover repository-neutral fixtures, bounded Windows transport paths, replay and mismatch rejection, and cleanup after a wrong-target rejection; the focused wrong-target test passed.
Brain Portability documentation distinguishes the one-time legacy bootstrap from reusable N-to-N+1 migrate-primary and identifies explicit reviewed BP-9 downstream adoption as the next consumer.
